-- Marginal tok/s by hour of day over the last week, with the slow tail
-- called out separately: p50 hides what users actually feel.

CREATE TABLE runs (
    id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    started_at  TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
    model       TEXT NOT NULL,
    concurrency INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    tokens      INTEGER NOT NULL,
    elapsed_ms  INTEGER NOT NULL
);

/* Corrections arrive as a new row with the same run id and a later
   ingested_at; the view below keeps only the latest of each. */
CREATE TABLE run_corrections (
    run_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES runs(id),
    tokens      INTEGER NOT NULL,
    elapsed_ms  INTEGER NOT NULL,
    ingested_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

INSERT INTO runs (started_at, model, concurrency, tokens, elapsed_ms)
VALUES ('2026-09-17 09:00:00', 'glm-4.7-q4', 4, 8192, 61000);

SELECT
    date_trunc('hour', r.started_at)              AS hour,
    count(*)                                      AS runs,
    round(avg(r.tokens * 1000.0 / r.elapsed_ms), 1) AS avg_tok_s,
    max(r.tokens * 1000.0 / r.elapsed_ms)           AS peak_tok_s
FROM runs r
WHERE r.started_at >= now() - INTERVAL '7 days'
  AND r.concurrency > 1
GROUP BY 1
HAVING count(*) >= 3
ORDER BY hour DESC
LIMIT 48;
